Product nuances: lead with Damask rose water/oil and medicinal extracts into India (India is a cumin exporter itself, so cumin is dead there) and into perfumery buyers; Iranian rose is a genuine quality-reputation asset (Fars-region high-geraniol oil), but rose OIL faces Turkey+Bulgaria who hold 80%+ of world output. Premium EU/perfumery demand (Germany, France, Switzerland) is real but now payment-hard - route it through a UAE or Bulgaria intermediary rather than direct. The US, UK, Canada and Australia are effectively CLOSED to Iranian-origin goods despite large demand - skip them. One supply-side red flag to resolve BEFORE committing volume: Iran imposed a temporary ban on all food/agricultural exports in early 2026 (Strait of Hormuz/conflict), with spices and herbs still leaking out under exporter pressure - secure supply, licences and origin paperwork first. Evidence: Iran non-oil to UAE ~$5.2B/8mo and to Iraq ~$8.3B/8mo (2024); Iran agri-exports +35% to ~$7.6B in 1403; essential-oil importers 2024 US $619M, France $140M, China $108M, India $95M; Iran is the world's largest rose-water producer (~70% of world rose).

countries.iran_angle: test

countries.why_import: World's largest date importer — roughly 437k MT in 2024 rising toward 458k MT by 2028, about $267M in 2023, and still growing. Soft/wet dates come mainly from UAE, Iran and Iraq; huge Muslim + festive/Ramadan consumption plus a fast-rising health-snack (date syrup/bars) segment.
countries.iran_angle: Iran already holds ~10.4% of India's date market and is THE reference supplier for soft juicy dates — 'Kimia', the standard Indian retail name for the product, literally IS Mazafati/Bam dates, so brand pull is pre-built. India's 10-year Chabahar terminal deal (May 2024) + INSTC give Iran a direct sea/land lane that bypasses UAE, and long-standing rupee-rial settlement keeps payment workable under sanctions. Best overall opportunity.
countries.demand_signal: India named the world's biggest date importer in 2025; Iran = 10.41% of India's date imports 2024-25; India-Iran FY24-25 trade ~$1.68B with Chabahar operationalized.

countries.why_import: Iran's 2nd-largest export market overall; foodstuffs are a core category and Iran already supplies ~20% of Iraq's consumer market. Strong Ramadan date demand plus a deep halva/ardeh (tahini) sweet-tooth culture, so both the dates AND the ardeh sell.
countries.iran_angle: Shared land border with established truck lanes (Mehran/Shalamcheh) means no shipping and fast delivery; dinar/informal and barter payment channels route around banking sanctions entirely. Iran is already embedded in Iraqi retail, and Mazafati + date bars + ardeh all match local taste. Lowest-friction real market.
countries.demand_signal: Iran-Iraq trade ~$12B in the year to Mar 2025 (target $20B); Iran's non-oil exports to Iraq hit $10B in the first 10 months of 2025.

countries.why_import: A top-5/6 destination for Iranian dates and a large sweets/halva-consuming market that imports most of its fruit. Both countries are Western-sanctioned, so they are politically aligned to trade with each other.
countries.iran_angle: The INSTC 'sanctions-proof' corridor (Caspian shipping + rail via Astrakhan) was built precisely for this flow; ruble-rial settlement and Mir-linked payment avoid Western banking. Iran competes on price against Tunisia/Egypt and benefits from Moscow actively pushing corridor volumes. Strong on both demand and payment navigability.
countries.demand_signal: INSTC 2024 freight 26.9M tons (+19% vs 2019), Moscow targeting 30M tons in 2025; Iran-Russia trade turnover topped $4B at end-2024.

countries.why_import: #2 destination for Iranian dates (~11% share) and the world's premier re-export hub — buys to repackage and re-ship onward to the GCC, Africa and even Western shelves under UAE origin.
countries.iran_angle: Short Persian Gulf hop (Bandar Abbas to Jebel Ali), thousands of Iranian trading firms already established in Dubai, and AED payment via free-zone banking that stays navigable. UAE is the main way Iranian dates legally re-origin to reach otherwise-blocked Western markets. CAVEAT: Iran-UAE ties are deteriorating into 2026 — treat as strong-but-monitor.
countries.demand_signal: Iran non-oil exports to UAE $7.2B in the year to Mar 2025; ~one-third of Iran's trade transits Dubai; Dubai FMCG re-export hub still growing in 2025.

countries.why_import: #5 destination for Iranian dates (~4.9% share); a Central Asian Muslim market with Ramadan demand and little domestic warm-climate fruit production of its own.
countries.iran_angle: Fast-improving Caspian + rail corridor — Kazakhstan-Iran rail freight jumped +69% in 2025 and bilateral trade +26.4% to $430M with a $3B roadmap. Iran is the natural cheap date supplier for landlocked Central Asia, and tenge/barter neighbor-corridor payments work around banking.
countries.demand_signal: Kazakhstan-Iran trade +26.4% to $430.2M in 2025; North-South corridor cargo +12% to 3.5M tons; 40 China-Iran cargo trains dispatched by end-2025 vs 7 in the prior seven years.

countries.why_import: #3 destination for Iranian dates (~7-11% share); enormous Ramadan consumption, a large population, and a shared Baloch date culture across the border.
countries.iran_angle: Direct land border (Taftan/Rimdan) with heavy informal cross-border trade; Iran is the nearest cheap soft-date source. CAVEAT: Iran-Pakistan banking is broken — alternative payment adds 3-5% and creates FX/pricing friction; volume is real but margins are squeezed. Barter mechanisms are being built to fix this.
countries.demand_signal: Global date sales spike +300% during Ramadan with Pakistan a top buyer; 2025 trade reporting flags banking restrictions adding 3-5% to Iran-Pakistan date deals.

countries.why_import: Small domestic market but strategically wide open, and a re-export/transit node into the Caucasus, Black Sea and beyond. Iran already supplies ~85% of Georgia's dates.
countries.iran_angle: This is go4it's live buyer lane already. Georgia is deliberately sanctions-navigable — thousands of Iranian firms are registered there, company setup is trivial, and USD/GEL banking still processes Iranian-origin goods. Low barrier to entry and a springboard for onward shipments; the ardeh/tahini add-on rides the same trucks.
countries.demand_signal: Iran = 85% of Georgia's date supply; Georgia's imports from Iran ~$230M (Jan-Nov 2025); thousands of Iranian companies operating in Georgia flagged in 2025 sanctions-evasion reporting.

countries.why_import: #4 destination for Iranian dates (~6.8% share) and a major halva/tahini and confectionery producer that imports raw dates and sesame inputs, then re-exports finished sweets to the EU and Gulf.
countries.iran_angle: Land border with established truck lanes (Bazargan/Gurbulak) and lira/barter trade; Iran feeds Turkey's processing industry cheaply. CAVEAT: Turkey is itself a leading tahini/halva exporter, so on finished ardeh you compete with locals — the real opening is Mazafati + raw/semi-processed inputs, not finished ardeh.
countries.demand_signal: Turkey among Iran's top-4 date buyers in 2024; Turkey-Iran trade sizeable ($3.2B+ Turkey to Iran in 2024) with an active food lane.

countries.why_import: Neighbor with steady basic-food demand; Iran is Afghanistan's single most important trade partner (~$3B/yr), and 2025 Pakistan-border closures pushed even more Afghan trade onto Iranian routes.
countries.iran_angle: Pure land lane via Dogharoun (handles ~60% of Iran's exports to Afghanistan) — cheap trucking, afghani/barter payment. CAVEAT: low-value, highly price-sensitive market with weak banking, and Afghanistan grows its own dried fruit — a thin-margin volume play only, not a premium Mazafati market.
countries.demand_signal: Iran non-oil exports to Afghanistan $1.156B in H1 2025 (+7% YoY); >$3B/yr through the Dogharoun crossing; Afghan trade actively rerouted through Iran in 2025.

blocked: United States — the tempting one: #1 tahini importer in the world and a huge date-bar/energy-snack market. Food/agriculture from Iran is technically the TSRA exception, BUT dollar-clearing banks, importer reluctance, FDA/importer registration and the general embargo make it effectively closed to a small Iranian-origin exporter. Do not chase.

European Union — Sept 2025 UN snapback triggered EU reimposition: the Central Bank of Iran and major Iranian banks are re-frozen and fund transfers to/from Iranian financial institutions are banned (de-minimis only ~EUR 10k). Food can in theory be licensed, but the payment channel is dead. Reach EU shelves only via UAE/Turkey re-origin, not directly.
United Kingdom — joined the 2025 snapback with parallel sanctions and the same banking wall against Iranian financial institutions; no workable direct payment lane.
Canada — broad, long-standing Iran sanctions plus importer/vendor-registration barriers; not navigable for Iranian-origin food.

Saudi Arabia — even after the 2023 detente there's no normal trade lane for Iranian-origin food, Iranian goods struggle to get local vendor registration, and Saudi is itself a top date producer/exporter (direct competitor). Not worth pursuing.
Israel — zero trade with Iran (hostile state); complete non-starter, listed only to be explicit.
products.summary: Iran is the world's #1 date exporter (~332k MT, ~$213M in 2024, +25% YoY) and Mazafati/Bam is its signature soft date (~180k MT, ~20% of date exports). The real money is NOT in the big Western date-bar/tahini markets (US is the #1 tahini importer, EU/US love date snacks) because Iranian origin is effectively banking-blocked there. The winnable opportunity clusters in three bands: (1) Big Muslim-population importers where Iran already has share and a lane — India (biggest date importer on earth, "Kimia" IS Mazafati) and Iraq (neighbor, ~20% of consumer market, halva/ardeh culture); (2) sanctions-aligned/corridor markets — Russia (INSTC, ruble) and Kazakhstan (Caspian/rail boom); (3) proximity + re-export hubs — UAE (Jebel Ali repack-and-reship), Georgia (go4it's live lane, 85% of its dates already Iranian), Pakistan (Ramadan, but broken banking), plus watch-list Turkey and Afghanistan. Rank drivers: existing Iranian share + an established corridor + a payment channel that survives sanctions. Ardeh/tahini demand is real but concentrates in Iraq/Levant/GCC (halva) and as processing input to Turkey — the Western tahini boom is mostly closed to Iran. Ship Mazafati + date bars as the volume drivers; treat ardeh as an add-on into Iraq/GCC/Georgia.

products.fa: کاشی و سرامیک و چینی بهداشتی

countries.why_import: Largest single market for Iranian tile/ceramic and sanitary ware by far. Post-war reconstruction + urbanization drive huge demand for cheap building materials; Iran's ceramic exports to Iraq were ~US$240M in 2022 and Iraq now takes an estimated 70-73% of ALL Iranian tile/ceramic exports. Iran also holds ~11% of Iraq's plastic sanitary-ware imports.
countries.iran_angle: Proximity + land route (trucks via Mehran/Basra/Shalamcheh) crush freight cost; Persian tile aesthetics are culturally aligned; deep existing trade lane and dinar/informal settlement channels already handle billions in Iranian non-oil goods, so payment and sanctions friction is effectively solved. This is the anchor account.
countries.demand_signal: 2025 reconstruction/urban projects still lifting building-material demand; IndexBox and Iranian trade press flag Iraq as the dominant, still-growing buyer for both tile and toilet articles.

countries.why_import: Iran is the single largest exporter of goods to Afghanistan; building materials (cement, TILES, ceramics, steel) are among Iran's main exports. Iran's non-oil exports to Afghanistan hit ~US$1.07B in just H1 of 2024, +28% by weight YoY. Reconstruction + almost no domestic tile/sanitary production means near-total import reliance.
countries.iran_angle: Shared land border (Islam Qala/Dogharoun) = cheapest possible truck freight for a heavy, low-value-per-kg product; Iran already dominates the supply base. 2025 Taliban-Pakistan border shutdowns pushed Afghan importers to lean even harder on the Iran corridor. Payment is informal/hawala/barter, which sidesteps banking sanctions entirely.
countries.demand_signal: Afghan-Pakistan trade contracted sharply and was periodically halted in 2025, redirecting construction-material sourcing toward Iran and Central Asia.

countries.why_import: Large construction sector, sanctioned off Western/EU tile supply, and actively substituting toward friendly suppliers. Iranian tile/porcelain-slab exports to Russia hit a new peak in 2025; ceramics are now a named key line in Iran's export basket to Russia; bilateral trade rose ~11% in H1 2025.
countries.iran_angle: Sanctions-navigable by design: both countries are sanctioned, so trade runs on rial-ruble / non-SWIFT channels and joint banking mechanisms rather than dollar clearing. The INSTC corridor (Caspian shipping now, Rasht-Astara rail due ~mid-2026) is being purpose-built to move exactly this kind of bulk cargo. Iran wins on price + a Western-vendor vacuum in the Russian market.
countries.demand_signal: Multiple 2025 Iranian trade sources report record tile/slab shipments to Russia and framing ceramics as a corridor-priority export.

countries.why_import: Growing residential/commercial construction with limited domestic tile capacity; imports Iranian tiles specifically for affordability + acceptable quality. Grouped with Turkey/Georgia/Armenia among Iran's largest tile destinations (that cluster is cited at ~74% of Iran's tile export value).
countries.iran_angle: Direct land border (Astara/Bilesuvar) = low freight; established cross-border trade and cultural/linguistic ties; no Western-style sanctions barrier on receiving Iranian-origin goods. Reliable neighbor account with room to grow.
countries.demand_signal: 2025 Iranian tile-market analyses list Azerbaijan among the steady top-tier neighbor buyers driven by construction demand.

countries.why_import: State-driven construction/urban build-out (Ashgabat and new-city projects) with little domestic ceramic industry; recurring buyer of Iranian tiles for infrastructure and housing.
countries.iran_angle: Shared border and rail: Iran and Turkmenistan agreed in 2025 to build two new rail lines at the Sarakhs crossing specifically to ease freight congestion and boost rail trade. Proximity + rail = strong logistics edge. UAE also re-exports ~US$1B/yr into Turkmenistan, so an Iran-direct lane undercuts that on cost.
countries.demand_signal: 2025 Iran-Turkmenistan Sarakhs rail expansion agreement signals rising freight volumes on this corridor.

countries.why_import: Fast-growing economy and construction boom; Iran's non-oil exports to Uzbekistan jumped +59.2% in value to US$353M and +80% in volume (Mar-Oct 2025). Building materials ride that surge.
countries.iran_angle: Rising, sanctions-tolerant lane via Turkmenistan/Central Asia; Iranian price competitiveness. HONEST CAVEAT: Uzbekistan is itself one of the region's larger tile producers, so the ceiling is capped and the real opening is in premium/porcelain and sanitary ware rather than commodity floor tile.
countries.demand_signal: Trend.az/Iran customs: +59% value, +80% volume growth in Iran-Uzbekistan non-oil trade for 7M2025 — one of the steepest regional growth rates.

countries.why_import: Steady residential and hospitality construction demand; consistently listed in the Turkey/Georgia/Armenia cluster that absorbs the bulk of Iran's tile export value; buys Iranian tile for durable, low-cost residential projects.
countries.iran_angle: No sanctions barrier to Iranian-origin goods; open, trade-friendly regime and a re-export/transit gateway toward the Black Sea and beyond. Reachable by land via Armenia/Azerbaijan. Good diversification and a potential onward-transit node.
countries.demand_signal: 2025 analyses note Georgia's demand for Iranian tiles growing steadily, weighted to residential.

countries.why_import: Large population and construction demand, and Iranian construction materials (tiles, cement, iron) already flow across the border. But Pakistan has its own protected tile industry and leans anti-import, so formal demand for foreign tile is thin.
countries.iran_angle: The real, resilient opportunity is the Balochistan/Sistan land-border barter trade (Taftan/Gabd), which runs largely outside formal banking and 'flourishes against the odds.' Iran wins purely on border-adjacent price. Treat as an informal border play, not a national-distribution market; formal banking + local protectionism cap anything bigger.
countries.demand_signal: Iran-Pakistan border trade in construction materials continued through 2024-2025 despite friction; growth is concentrated at the frontier, not in formal ports.

countries.why_import: Not primarily an end-consumer of Iranian tile, but the region's dominant transshipment/blending/re-export hub — Iran sent ~US$7.2B of non-oil goods to the UAE in FY2024/25, much of it re-exported onward (incl. ~US$1B/yr of UAE goods into Turkmenistan alone).
countries.iran_angle: Value is as a GATEWAY, not a destination: Dubai/Sharjah traders re-flag and re-invoice Iranian-origin goods to reach GCC/Africa/South Asia buyers who won't import directly from Iran. Short Persian Gulf shipping hop, mature Iranian merchant network. CAVEAT: UAE enforces product registration and periodically tightens on Iranian re-exports, so margins/route depend on the re-export partner, not on selling 'Iranian origin' openly.
countries.demand_signal: 2025 Tehran Times/TV BRICS: Iran-UAE non-oil trade at multi-billion run-rate with the UAE explicitly functioning as re-export intermediary.

blocked: United States — Comprehensive OFAC embargo (31 CFR Part 560): U.S. persons are barred from purchasing, transporting, financing or brokering ANY Iranian-origin goods, with construction-sector materials specifically named. Zero legal path; do not chase.

European Union — Even where tiles aren't item-specifically sanctioned, SWIFT/banking cutoff, secondary-sanctions risk on EU importers, and powerful domestic producers (Italy, Spain, Portugal, Poland — plus an active anti-dumping regime against other origins) mean no EU distributor will register or clear Iranian-origin ceramic. Effectively closed.
United Kingdom — Aligned with EU/US sanctions and banking restrictions on Iranian-origin trade; same practical closure as the EU.
Canada — Broad Iran sanctions and banking prohibitions make Iranian-origin building materials non-importable.

Saudi Arabia — Despite the 2023 diplomatic thaw, still effectively closed: SASO/SABER vendor-registration and conformity barriers, banking friction, and Saudi Arabia's own status as a top-3 regional tile producer block Iranian-origin building materials from the formal channel. Any entry would have to route via UAE re-export, not direct.

India — Not sanctions-blocked but pointless to pursue: India is the world's #2 tile EXPORTER (a direct competitor, not a buyer) and Iran-India banking (post-rupee-account wind-down) is friction-heavy. No real import demand for Iranian tile.
products.summary: Iran-origin tiles/ceramics + sanitary ware sell where three things line up: real construction demand, a land or Caspian corridor that makes heavy low-value cargo economic, and a payment/sanctions path that avoids dollar clearing. That points overwhelmingly at neighbors and fellow-sanctioned states, not open Western markets. TIER 1 (anchor the book here): Iraq — the dominant market at ~70-73% of all Iranian tile/ceramic exports (~$240M+/yr), reconstruction-driven, land-routed, payment already solved; Afghanistan — Iran is its #1 supplier of building materials, near-total import reliance, cheapest possible truck freight, informal payment, and 2025 Pakistan-border shutdowns funneling more demand to the Iran lane; Russia — record 2025 tile/slab shipments into a Western-vendor vacuum, built on the INSTC corridor and rial-ruble settlement, the biggest upside story. TIER 2 (solid neighbor/corridor accounts): Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan (bordering, rail-connected, price-led), Uzbekistan (fastest-growing lane, +59% value in 2025, but caps out on commodity tile because it produces its own — push porcelain/sanitary ware), and Georgia (steady residential demand + onward-transit gateway, no sanctions barrier). TIER 3 / structural: Pakistan is a frontier-barter play only (formal market is protectionist), and the UAE matters as a re-export GATEWAY to reach buyers who won't touch Iranian origin directly — not as an end market. AVOID: the US, EU, UK, Canada are legally/financially closed to Iranian-origin goods; Saudi Arabia is practically closed via SASO registration + domestic production despite the political thaw; India is a competitor-exporter, not a buyer. Net: win on price + proximity + sanctions-navigable settlement in the neighborhood; don't burn effort on the big Western markets.
